svg.title: Noctium project goals: the full native Midnight capability map
svg.desc: Research preview. Six project goals cover full native ZKIR v3, the Lean contract language, ledger capabilities and composition, private execution and disclosure, native/web/mobile SDKs, and proof-to-deployment assurance. These are target capabilities, not a list of delivered features. Current evidence covers claim-specific correctness and scoped privacy, exact byte/build certificates, Rust and C/C++ private-claim proving, transactions and recovery on localnet. Twenty-seven opcode names have restricted source-producer support. Native examples cover guarded state effects, nested maps, Native-field records and Bytes32 account hashes, ordered domain-separated vector hashes and canonical Native-field hashes. Typed Jubjub examples check byte-derived keys, ElGamal binding and ECDH memo recovery against native execution, not a new proof or deployment. Native and JubjubScalar field inversion has a focused native check. This count does not establish complete overload coverage. Generic scalar lowerer soundness and completeness are proved. Frontend preservation, broader native proofs, capabilities and web/mobile SDKs remain open. The selected claim has qualified deployed identity.

g.text: Noctium
RESEARCH PREVIEW
Prove contract behavior. Target the full native Midnight stack.
Lean 4 compiler and proofs · Direct native backend · No Compact dependency or scope ceiling
PROJECT GOALS
Target capabilities below. Current evidence covers selected programs.
Full native ZKIR v3
Lean contract language
Ledger capabilities + composition
Private execution + disclosure
Native, web and mobile SDKs
Proof-to-deployment assurance
47 instruction variants · 15 native value types · ZKIR 3.2.1
Typed source mappings · canonical encodings · cryptography
Native checking · key generation · proving · verification
Execution evidence and explicit upstream blockers
Scalars · composite values · functions and typed helpers
Modules · generics · bounded loops · guarded control
Circuit constraints separate from ledger state transitions
Ordinary Lean specifications, theorems and tactics
Cells · maps · sets · lists · Merkle trees · nested ADTs
Constructors · sealed fields · native Kernel effects
Contract calls and composability · events · assets
Bound call statements, state effects and failure behavior
Private witnesses · host providers · private-state lifecycle
Value and control-flow tracking · guarded disclosure
Explicit authorized releases and privacy observers
Native funding, submission, journals and recovery
Native applications: Rust + C/C++ host ABI
Browser dapps: TypeScript + portable WASM
Android: Kotlin · iOS: Swift
Shared artifacts and conformance vectors across hosts
Actual-source correctness, invariants and scoped privacy
Compiler preservation · completeness · kernel/axiom audits
Exact builds and artifacts · keys and deployed operations
Explicit trust assumptions and independent review
PUBLISHED EVIDENCE
27 opcode names · scoped source support · tagged SHA-256
Native state + derived keys · ElGamal + ECDH memos
Claim + scalar proofs · localnet · Rust + C/C++ clients
OPEN ASSURANCE + COVERAGE
Full ZKIR v3 · other curves + contract composition
Mixed state + token integration · broader compiler proofs
TypeScript/WASM, Kotlin and Swift SDKs
